translation:
Above-rising qi, panting and rapid (chuanji), is hardest to treat; breathing uneven and irregular, the state is pitiable. Lung replete with heat-pathogen, it swells and hastens; lung deficient with cold, it is timid in its faintness.
Hands and feet warm — therein a thread of life; the four limbs cold, in dreams no doubt. Dingchuan Tang (Settle-the-Panting Decoction) head, weigh and use; cloud, mud, tiger, rat — truly a hair's breadth apart (life and death).
Dingchuan Tang (Settle-the-Panting) with Fuling (Poria) and Suzhi (Perilla seed) and Gua (Gualou/Fruitful Trichosanthes); Chenpi (Tangerine), Baiguo (Ginkgo) and Kuandonghua (Tussilago). Gancao (Licorice), Mahuang (Ephedra), Sangbai (Mulberry Root Bark) and Xing (Xingren/Apricot Kernel); Chenxiang (Aquilaria) and Banxia (Pinellia), praised from antiquity.
translator_notes: 云泥虎鼠=cloud-vs-mud, tiger-vs-mouse: extremes of auspicious/ominous fate.
book: 七十二症辨治方法（手抄本）

translation:
As to roaring/panting-with-whistle (xiaohou), originally it is the phlegm of the lung orifice, and again because of external heat wrapping internal cold. The throat day and night has no ceasing sound; the voice and timbre are strange, like a plucked string.
The heart polluted with floating-smooth (pulse) is cured by decoction or pill; long treatment, deep-hesitant (pulse), seek the efficacious elixir. Treat the panting (xiao) with a decoction-head combining dispersing the exterior; do not need many methods, rashly spoken.
Dingxiao Tang (Settle-the-Roaring-Panting Decoction) uses Renshen (Ginseng) and Ejiao (Ass-Hide Gelatin); Mahuang (Ephedra), Gancao (Licorice) and Sangbai (Mulberry Root Bark) added. Wuwei (Schisandra), Banxia (Pinellia) and Yingsuqiao (Poppy Capsule); facing the moment, respond and change — then it is best.
translator_notes: 哮吼=roaring panting (asthma-like); 定哮湯=Dingxiao Tang.
book: 七十二症辨治方法（手抄本）

translation:
Why do many names of the malaria disease exist? No need for many methods to waste the heart in vain; always it is interior injury and exterior contraction; when interior and exterior both lose guard, malaria comes to invade.
Pathogen and proper not separated, cold and heat erupt; yin and yang alternately closed off, it achieves the reversal. The Classics say without phlegm there is no malaria; the source of the spleen and stomach can be purified and cleared.
Wiry and rapid (pulse), more heat — must resolve by sweat; wiry and slow (pulse), much cold — must warm and level. Without sweat one should sweat and disperse the pathogen qi; with sweat one should stop it and seek the proper qi.
Chailing (Bupleurum-Poria) both separate and clear the exterior and interior; Qingpi (Clear-the-Spleen) without obstruction is wonderful as a spirit. Although Guikun Lidan (Ghost-Cry Magic Elixir) is a cut-short method, in the deficiency/excess and new/stale one must distinguish clearly.
Within Sanxie Tang (Disperse-the-Pathogen Decoction) there is Mahuang (Ephedra); Fangfeng (Ledebouriella), Jing-Ai (Schizonepeta) and Qianghuo all complete. Zisu (Perilla), Zhi (Baizhi), Shao (Peony) and Chuanxiong and Gancao (Licorice); at length the malaria sweat pours in two basins.
Chailing Tang (Bupleurum-Poria Decoction) is the name of the two decoctions (Chaihu + Wuling); distinguishing yin and yang, ask new and stale; harmonizing and resolving malaria, unblocking the exterior and interior, without arrogance, without flattery rejoicing in peace and ascent.
Qingpi (Clear-the-Spleen) Gancao (Licorice), Guo (Caoguo/Black Cardamom) and Fuling (Poria); Baizhu (Atractylodes), Qingpi (Green Tangerine), Houpu and Qin (Scutellaria). Banxia (Pinellia), Chaihu (Bupleurum) and Gancao (Licorice) as companions; the Great Yin (Taiyin) malaria demon wanders the mountain forest.

More heat than cold, bitter mouth, dry throat, stool and urine both red and rough, pulse coming wiry and rapid — this formula governs it.

Now qingpi (clearing the spleen) is not to be taken as cool-clearing. Rather it is attacking and removing the pathogen, so the middle jiao becomes clear after all. Therefore Qingpi and Houpu clear away the phlegm in the spleen. Banxia and Fuling clear away the dampness in the spleen. Chaihu and Huangqin clear away the heat in the spleen. Baizhu and Gancao clear away the deficiency in the spleen. And Caoguoren (Black Cardamom) in turn clears the illness of the gaohuang (vitals).

Qibao Yin (Seven-Precious Beverage)
Changshan (Dichroa), Houpu, Chenpi, Gancao, Binglang (Areca), Caoguo, equal parts, decoct in wine, leave overnight in the open, warm-take next morning.
This formula is usable when the pulse comes floating-large, wiry-smooth; if hesitant, fine and faint, do not use.

Sanjie Tang (Three-Resolve Decoction)
Chaihu (Bupleurum), Zexie (Alisma), Mahuang (Ephedra, de-knotted)
This is a formula treating malaria when in season the young and old (of a region) present similar symptoms — it governs them. This formula can only drain the replete; the deficient should supplement their qi and blood.

Cut-Malaria Proven Formula
Changshan three qian, Binglang one qian, Caoguo one grain, Cangzhu one qian, Banxia one qian, Houpu eight fen, Qingpi one qian, Chaihu eight fen, Wumei five grains, Hongzao three grains, Cong three stalks, Dengxin seven strips, Shengjiang three slices, two bowls of water decoct to one bowl.
On the appointed day in the early morning, face east, feet standing evenly, take it and it is removed.
translator_notes: 柴苓湯=Chailing Tang (Chaihu+Wuling); 清脾湯=Qingpi Tang; 七寶飲=Qibao Yin; 三解湯=Sanjie Tang.
book: 七十二症辨治方法（手抄本）
